method: Hand audit of every flow the lineage graph reported for the natural JS/TS units (express/examples, fastify/examples; the two lib roots report no flows). The labeller read the pinned source at the cited file and line and recorded which request field actually reaches the response, redirect or log sink that the flow ends in. The flows were listed first and then audited, so these labels are NOT independent of the scanner output: they judge the flows it reported, and say nothing about flows it did not report (that is the recall question, scored by labels/real.json). Matching key: unit id, source file, field name and the first source line of the reported flow.

verdicts.correct: the reported source field is the field that reaches the sink
verdicts.wrong-field: a flow reaches that sink, but from a different (sibling) field than the one reported
verdicts.no-flow: no request field reaches that sink; the reported flow does not exist

labels.evidence: from is an argument of names.slice(from, to + 1) whose result is joined into res.send
to is an argument of names.slice(from, to + 1) whose result is joined into res.send
id = req.params.user_id is concatenated into the res.redirect target
req.params.pid is concatenated into the res.send string of pets.delete
req.params.sub is concatenated into the res.send string
req.body.user is only copied into req.user.name and req.user.email; the redirect target is req.get('Referrer'), which does not read req.user
req.params.uid reaches res.send at lines 37, 47 and 51 (through escapeHtml)
console.log(request.params); the field is right, the reported source kind is not (request.params is a route parameter, not a model output)
